title: Irrigation.ltd launch note: planning before hardware
excerpt: A private editorial record of Irrigation.ltd’s planning-first introduction, its stated IAM attribution, and the limits of what the supplied homepage evidence proves.
intro: Irrigation.ltd introduces its purpose with a practical distinction: understand the landscape before choosing irrigation hardware. Its homepage presents guidance for people considering anything from a first garden bed to a whole property, with planning questions positioned ahead of equipment selection. This private launch note explains that editorial purpose. It is not evidence that an automated publishing workflow, enquiry route or interactive planning tool has passed a production test.

sections.heading: The starting point is the property
paragraphs: The homepage identifies home gardens, lawns and landscapes, and shared properties as its settings. Rather than presenting those settings as interchangeable installation jobs, it asks readers to begin with the spaces and plants they want to water.

Its planning sequence then expands the brief: note slopes, shade, soil and existing problems; check local watering and backflow requirements; and discuss flow, pressure and design with a professional. The editorial value is in organizing the questions that precede a technical decision—not in treating a general guide as a finished irrigation design.

sections.heading: Method selection comes before a shopping list
paragraphs: The homepage groups its introductory material around drip irrigation, sprinkler systems, smarter watering, and care and troubleshooting. Those categories give readers several ways into the subject: delivery near the root zone, coverage questions, observation of soil and weather, or an existing problem that needs attention.

The guide titles reinforce that planning emphasis. One compares drip, sprinklers and hand watering around plants, soil and daily routine. Another introduces the planning considerations for garden-bed drip irrigation, including emitters, filtration and root-zone coverage. A vegetable-garden guide directs attention to soil, plant stage and delivery pattern before changing a timer.
Read together, these topics establish a useful editorial boundary: choosing an approach and identifying unanswered questions are distinct from specifying a system.

sections.heading: A planning brief is not a system design
paragraphs: The page describes a useful project brief as a record of planting, water source, site conditions and unanswered questions. That makes the brief a preparation document for a later conversation, rather than evidence that the site supplies engineered plans or installation services.

The visual framing carries a similar limitation. The homepage labels its main illustration as conceptual, not a system design, and describes its guide artwork as original conceptual illustration. That distinction matters: an explanatory image should not be read as a layout someone can install.

sections.heading: Reader guidance and industry marketing are separate paths
paragraphs: The footer separates landscape resources from an industry-facing group of links labelled Contractor sign-up, Market with us, Guest posting and Business guides. It also states that the resource is powered by Industry Army Marketing, a division of BuildersHaus.com.

Those labels establish how the homepage presents its industry context; they do not demonstrate that any linked service or form works. An IAM marketing enquiry must remain distinct from a property owner’s request for irrigation advice or a contractor’s client enquiry. Nothing in the supplied evidence establishes contractor matching, enquiry delivery or ownership of a resulting customer relationship.

sections.heading: What this private record proves—and what remains unproven
paragraphs: The supplied homepage text supports the launch’s editorial proposition: irrigation guidance built around site observation, method comparison and preparation for a professional conversation. It also supports the stated parent attribution and the navigation labels described above.

It does not supply runtime receipts for publication, live rendering, working links, form submission, enquiry routing or automated generation. This article therefore records the launch presentation and its planning purpose, not a completed operational verification. A claim that those services operate would require separate functional evidence.
